newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil trader gave Japan politician donation - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Oil trader gave Japan politician donation - Kyodo.

text.p: A powerful Japanese politician received several million yen in political donations from an oil dealer arrested on suspicion of evading taxes, Kyodo news agency reported on Monday.
Quoting unnamed sources, Kyodo said a "powerful" incumbent Lower House legislator had received several million yen from millionaire oil wholesaler Junichi Izui. Kyodo did not name the politician.
The news agency said the politician did not report the donation in his tax return as required for politicians.
Izui, owner and sole employee of oil wholesaler Izui Oil Co, was arrested last Thursday on charges he evaded 310 million yen in taxes.
Izui handed over to investigation authorities a notebook in which he had recorded banquet dates and the names of 16 politicians, Kyodo said.
Also written in the notebook were the names of "many" bureaucrats from ministries including the powerful Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), it said.
Government officials declined to comment on the report and calls to Izui's office in Osaka went unanswered.

In a separate report over the weekend, Kyodo said the Osaka-based oil dealer wined and dined MITI officials and made legal political donations to at least five lawmakers, including Taku Yamasaki, the policy chief of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

In a news conference on Thursday after the first meeting of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new cabinet, new Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said he met Izui two or three times at fund-raising parties. "I believe I have not done anything illegal," he said.

LDP secretary-general Koichi Kato also said he met Izui at a private function a few years ago. Izui bought 200,000 yen worth of fund-raising party tickets, Kyodo said. But Kato denied having any specific relationship with him, Kyodo said.
